points.why: It covers the 2-3 year construction lag and says rents can't show the effect yet, but never mentions that rent data reflects leases signed months earlier.

It warns that repeal causes a later completions gap and that the all-at-once package hides what worked, but it never says that reacting harder to a late signal risks overcorrection when delayed supply lands on top of the new measures.
It asks for a dashboard of permits, starts and completions, and for a review date at 36-48 months with pre-agreed criteria instead of repealing now.
It says to change one thing at a time and to keep any interim measure narrow, and it names outside forces such as job and population demand and financing costs.
